theorem.statement: Resolution is not polynomial-time automatizable unless P=NP; more strongly, it is NP-hard to distinguish formulas having polynomial-size Resolution refutations from formulas having no subexponential-size Resolution refutations.
theorem.title: Automating Resolution is NP-Hard
theorem.venue: Journal of the ACM 67(5), Article 31 (2020); preliminary version FOCS 2019

direct_L3_consequence: A TRUMP L3 proof that says 'short Resolution refutations exist, therefore a deterministic polynomial procedure can find them' is invalid. Polynomial Resolution proof discovery would itself imply P=NP.
transfer_firewall: P_SIMULATION_OR_PROOF_SIZE_EQUIVALENCE_ALONE != AUTOMATIZABILITY_TRANSFER; any transfer to another proof language must preserve proof search effectively and be proved separately.

supporting_results.authors: Ian Mertz; Toniann Pitassi; Yuanhao Wei
supporting_results.title: Short Proofs Are Hard to Find
supporting_results.role: Additional conditional non-automatizability/hardness results for Resolution and related systems; not needed for the core unconditional NP-hardness statement used here.

next_L3_question: Choose one frozen proof language strictly beyond the already blocked Resolution-only route and prove either a polynomial-time discovery theorem or a search-hardness barrier for that exact language. No heuristic selector and no proof-size-only argument is admissible.
